settings.headline:
Stand close.
Look slowly.
settings.copy: The White Room is a gallery built on a single conviction: great art rewards the people who stop rushing. We show a small, rigorously chosen rotation of contemporary painters and sculptors — and give every work the space, light, and silence it needs to do its work.

settings.title: Current
settings.intro: Each season we hang one show and one artist's solo work in the back gallery. Here's what's on the walls this month.

features.title: Mara Voss — 'Still, Between'
features.text: A solo show of large-scale charcoal works that read, from a distance, as pure black geometry — and up close dissolve into hours of patient, trembling line. On view in the main room through the end of the season.

features.title: The Quiet Object
features.text: A group show of sculpture and ceramics chosen for how they hold light and silence in a room: bronze, stone, and fired clay from four artists, arranged in a single long line down the east gallery.

features.title: New Drawings & Small Works
features.text: A rotating wall of affordable small works — drawings, studies, and editions — so that a first collection doesn't have to start with a big leap. Every piece is original, numbered, and priced clearly.

features.title: Open to the Public, Free Always
features.text: Admission is always free. We believe the work should be the only barrier to entry — never a ticket price. Guided conversations with the artists happen every first Thursday.

settings.title: The spaces that
settings.intro: A gallery is architecture for looking. Ours is a converted print works: high ceilings, north light, and floors worn smooth by decades of feet.

settings.title: Work that found
settings.intro: A few of the pieces that left our walls this season — and the quiet satisfaction of seeing them land in the right hands.

items.title: Mara Voss — 'Held', charcoal on paper
items.tag: Sold · placed in a private collection
items.text: A four-foot charcoal study of an empty chair, bought on the second day of the show by a collector who wrote that it 'looked like waiting.'

items.title: Kenji Aoki — 'Vessel No. 4', bronze
items.text: The fourth in a series of cast bronze vessels. The buyer commissioned a fifth before the fourth had even been crated.

items.title: A first collection, started small
items.text: A couple came in for one small drawing and left with three: the drawing, a study by the same artist, and a ceramic they couldn't stop returning to.

settings.title: The feeling of
settings.intro: People tell us the same thing: they came in for ten minutes and stayed for an hour. Here's a little of that.

reviews.quote: I walked in intending to stay five minutes and stayed two hours. The white room does something to the light that makes you stand still. I bought my first piece of original art that day — a small drawing from the study wall.
reviews.author: Dana Whitfield

reviews.quote: As an artist, the showing was a gift. They gave the work room to breathe, lit it honestly, and let it speak for itself. That's rarer than people know.
reviews.author: Mara Voss

reviews.quote: Admission is free, the staff never hover, and the curation is serious without being precious. This is exactly what a neighborhood gallery should be.
reviews.author: Elliot Reyes
